lines.text: You glance at your phone, and it unlocks. In the dark. With glasses on. How does it know it's you, and not a photo of you?
At the top of the screen, a tiny projector fires about thirty thousand invisible dots of infrared light onto your face.
Your eyes can't see them. But an infrared camera can. It photographs how the dots land on your nose, cheeks and eyes.
In the dark, an invisible flood light lights you up too. So it works with the lights off.
Dots on your nose land closer than dots on your cheeks. From that, the phone builds a 3D map of your face.
That's why a photo fails. A photo is flat. No nose sticking out, no depth.
The map is turned into math and kept in a sealed chip inside the phone. It never goes to the cloud.
Apple says the chance a random stranger unlocks your phone is about one in a million.
Same idea in Orbi Transfer. Your passcode never leaves your phone. And 30 minutes later, the file burns. Gone.
